chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:

I described to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the words of Hisham al-Jawaliqi and what he was saying regarding the fully-grown youth, and I described to him the words of Hisham ibn al-Hakam. So he said: 'Indeed, nothing resembles God.'

key_terms.الشَّابِّ الْمُوَفَّقِ: The 'guided/favoured youth' — a reference to the anthropomorphic image of God as a young man described by Hisham al-Jawaliqi
key_terms.الْجَوَالِيقِيِّ: Al-Jawaliqi — a theologian within early Islamic discourse who reportedly held anthropomorphic views about God
key_terms.لَا يُشْبِهُهُ شَيْءٌ: Nothing resembles Him — the core Quranic principle of divine incomparability (tanzih), echoing 42:11

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about those who compared God to a human youth?
ai.summary: This hadith records a brief but decisive theological statement by Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him), Abu al-Hasan. The narrator, Muhammad ibn Hakim, had presented to the Imam the anthropomorphic theological positions of Hisham al-Jawaliqi — who reportedly likened God to a youthful human form — and contrasted these with the more nuanced (but still reportedly problematic) views of Hisham ibn al-Hakam on divine attributes. The Imam responded with the foundational Shia theological principle drawn directly from the Quran (42:11): 'Indeed, nothing resembles God' — a categorical affirmation of divine transcendence and incomparability (tanzih) that rejects all forms of anthropomorphism (tashbih).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym who said,

‘I described to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the words of Hisham Al-Jawaliqy and what he is saying regarding the fully grown youth, and described to him<sup>asws</sup> the words of Hisham Bin Al-Hakam. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Surely Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, nothing resembles Him<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Iisa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following.

“I mentioned to abu al-Hassan al-Awwal (the first) (a.s.), the statements of Hisham al-Jawaliqi and what he says about fully grown up young man (see Hadith 3 Chapter on prohibited Attributes). I also mentioned the statements of Hisham ibn al-Hakam in this matter.” The Imam said, “Allah, certainly, is not similar to any thing.”
